protocol: §C.2.6 — 20 passages and 20 queries, top-10 entries annotated plausible / not
annotator_note: Single annotator (the study author), as §C.2.6 allows when a second is unavailable; reported as such. No inter-annotator agreement.
config: e5 / layer 9 / R2 / whitened / cell kd128_kq16_nnz120_log1p

not_plausible.why: the list is dominated by page boilerplate rather than the plant the passage is about

weak.why: the rare given name is out of V, so only 'name'/'meaning' are representable — a coverage limit, not an implausible list

qualitative_observations: Expansion is real, not just lexical echo: a nursing passage activates `midwives`, a cortisol passage activates `pituitary` and `gland`, a rash passage activates `ringworm` and `fungal`, a SWIFT-code passage activates `aba`.

Query lists are steep (top-1 carries 18.5% of the mass, participation ratio 14 of 30 non-zeros) while document lists are flat (top-1 3.5%, participation ratio 63 of 119). Untrained max-pooled cosine gives documents nearly uniform weights, so the score is spread over ~63 effective dimensions instead of concentrating on the discriminative ones. That asymmetry is the most likely reason the training-free run reaches only 0.51x BM25 despite plausible term lists, and it is exactly what Pilot D's learned threshold and scale exist to fix.
